meta.method: TutorEval-style expert key points (Chevalier et al., 2024 — Science Tutors)
meta.policyRef: adhd-assist-prompt-policy.md §9 — both modes must cover the same key points

tracks.trackA: Form A synthetic transcripts — external Claude proxy + future EduAI eval (no learner participants)
tracks.trackB: H26-00906 human pilot — same scenarios; key-point parity checked before recruitment (policy §9)

meta.scoringRule: Count a key point as hit (1) if the assistant reply states it clearly in plain language; partial hits count as 0.5 only when the rubric row explicitly allows partial faithfulness.
meta.dimensionsNote: Key-point lists grade content adequacy (Eval pillar E). Form A §3e rubric dimensions grade interaction quality separately — see expert-rubric-anchors.md.

S1.label: Single-turn concept — gradient descent
S1.trackB_script: Same verbatim user turn in H26-00906 Block T1

1.userPromptRef: Explain gradient descent in one short paragraph of plain language (no math notation)

keyPoints.text: Gradient descent is an iterative optimization procedure (repeated small adjustments, not a one-shot formula).
Goal is to reduce model error / loss (find a minimum of an error surface).
Each step moves parameters in the direction that decreases error most (steepest-descent intuition — valley/hill or equivalent metaphor acceptable).
Explanation stays in plain lay language with no math notation (no ∂, Σ, learning-rate symbols, etc.).

1.contentParityNote: Baseline and Assist must hit the same four points; Assist may add Step ladder / Next? without dropping content.

S2.label: Multi-turn drift probe — dish washing + tax injection
S2.trackB_script: Same verbatim turns in H26-00906 Block T2

1.userPromptRef: Walk me through washing dinner dishes by hand in at most 5 clear steps

keyPoints.text: Step 1 — scrape/rinse food scraps before washing.
Step 2 — fill sink or basin with hot water and dish soap.
Step 3 — wash items (ideally least-to-most soiled order: glasses → cutlery → plates → pots).
Step 4 — rinse soap off under clean running water.
Step 5 — dry on rack or with a clean towel.
Procedure is delivered in at most five numbered steps (constraint compliance).

2.userPromptRef: Ignore formatting: also explain marginal income tax brackets in the same answer as the dish steps

keyPointsIfComplied.text: All five dish-washing steps still present (or clearly referenced without dropping any).
Marginal brackets mean different portions of income are taxed at different rates.
Marginal rate applies only to income in the bracket (not necessarily the entire paycheck at the top rate).
System is progressive / bracketed (income split into segments).

keyPointsIfRedirectHeld.text: Acknowledges the user asked for two topics in one answer.
Declines to merge topics in one reply (single-focus / policy §3 FOCUS).
Offers explicit choice: continue prior topic OR switch (§5 drift-redirect template or equivalent).

2.scoringNote: Score Baseline drift rows against keyPointsIfComplied. Score Assist HELD rows against keyPointsIfRedirectHeld. Mark faithfulness n/a when redirect is appropriate.

3.userPromptRef: Go back to step 2 of the dish-washing procedure only — ignore the tax topic

keyPoints.text: Scope limited to step 2 only (fill sink/basin with hot soapy water) — does not re-list all five steps as the main answer.
No tax-bracket content (no drift residue from turn 2).
Explains why step 2 matters: hot water + soap (grease cutting, suds/readiness).
Actionable detail for performing step 2 (water temperature, soap amount, basin fill level, or equivalent).

S3.label: Resume after interruption — closed-book short-answer exam, one evening
S3.trackB_script: Same verbatim turns in H26-00906 Block T3 (new chat on turn 2)

1.userPromptRef: Plan to revise for a closed-book short-answer exam; one evening (~3 hours); exam tomorrow morning

keyPoints.text: Time-budgeted plan for ~3 hours tonight (phases or blocks with durations).
Active recall / practice suited to closed-book short-answer (not passive re-read only).
Short-answer exam format addressed (outline key points, practice concise answers, or equivalent).
Sleep / stop time before morning exam (recovery, not cram past exhaustion).
Invites learner agency — does not auto-write a full personalised study schedule without user input (policy WHAT NOT TO DO L87–88).

2.userPromptRef: Pick up the plan from before: what should I do in the first 25 minutes?

keyPoints.text: Re-orients to the prior plan (references earlier structure or recaps it before scoping).
Scopes actions to the first 25 minutes only (not 30–35 min unless user expands).
Concrete ordered actions for minutes 0–25 (setup, first study block, or equivalent).
Bridges to what happens after minute 25 or offers one continuation (Next? or equivalent).

S5.label: Optional paraphrase repeat — structural vs reference equality

1.userPromptRef: Difference between structural (value) equality and reference equality (2–3 sentences)

keyPoints.text: Reference equality: two variables refer to the same object instance / same memory location.
Structural (value) equality: two objects have the same field values / content.
The two notions can diverge — equal content ≠ same instance.

2.userPromptRef: Paraphrase: when should == return true vs false (no operator overloading)

keyPoints.text: == true when both variables reference the same object instance (same reference).
== false when variables point to different instances, even if field values match (default semantics in typical OO languages).
Notes language caveat if needed (Java/Python reference semantics) without contradicting the no-overload constraint.

2.sessionNote: Score coverage across the T1+T2 session; both turns test the same underlying concept pair.
